thread:
Chloe Martin: Quick q for folks who weighed in on ENG-2408 / PR-18695 — what audit logging granularity do we want for Suggestions? Right now we log a single “suggestions.read” when the page loads. Do we need separate events for list vs detail drawer vs export? Also: any privacy concerns since savings/risk are cost/usage-derived?

Kaitlyn Nguyen: +1 to splitting. “Page load” is too fuzzy for audits. I’d want at minimum:
- suggestions.list_viewed (enter Suggestions view)
- suggestions.detail_viewed (user opens a specific suggestion id)
- suggestions.exported (if/when we add CSV / API export)

Kaitlyn Nguyen: Re privacy: audit logs shouldn’t include the values (e.g., $/1M tokens, projected monthly savings). Those are derived from usage and can be sensitive. Keep payload minimal: actor_id, tenant/workspace, route/model identifiers *if needed*, suggestion_id, action, and maybe schema_version.

Naomi Feldman: From security/compliance POV: anything that reveals spend/traffic patterns is “sensitive business data” for a bunch of customers (even if not PII). Agree: do NOT log numeric savings, confidence intervals, “basis of estimate” telemetry window, etc.

Naomi Feldman: We also need to be careful about “route” names if customers use internal identifiers (sometimes those leak product names). If you can avoid route strings in audit logs, do it. Suggestion_id + tenant + actor + action should be enough.

Marcus Lin: +1. Also watch for query params: filters can include model + region + route. If we log request URLs anywhere, make sure we’re not accidentally persisting query strings in audit pipeline.

Logan Wright: Volume note: if we log detail_viewed for every drawer open, that’s fine. But don’t log “row impression” / scroll events as audit logs. Keep audit logs to explicit user actions.

Logan Wright: Analytics events can capture impressions/clickthrough (ENG-2409), but audit logs should be “who accessed sensitive surface area” not product metrics.

Jada Williams: Agree on splitting list vs detail. I’d also distinguish UI vs API. Our BFF calls suggestions-service a lot (pagination, refresh, polling on focus). We should avoid logging internal service-to-service reads as “user did X” multiple times.

Jada Williams: Proposed rule: audit log only on Console edge when the request is tied to an end-user session AND is the first successful response for a given screen state. E.g.,
- list_viewed: first successful GET /suggestions for that session/page
- detail_viewed: first successful GET /suggestions/{id} per suggestion per session

Chloe Martin: That makes sense. For beta we don’t have export yet, but we might add “Copy suggestion ID” and “Open docs link” etc. Are those audit-worthy?

Kaitlyn Nguyen: Docs link no. Copy suggestion id probably no. The main compliance ask we’ve heard is: “Who accessed this optimization recommendation / cost analysis surface.” So list + detail + export are the big ones.

Allison Grant: On observability side: please don’t couple audit logging to retries. If suggestions-service 5xx and Console retries, you could spam audit logs unless it’s only on successful response as Jada said.

Naomi Feldman: Another nuance: RBAC failures should also be audited. If someone without permission attempts access, that’s a security signal. But payload should be minimal and not include suggestion content.

Ethan Park: What permission are we keying this off? Is it the same as “Optimize:View” or a new “Suggestions:View”? If it’s new, audit log should include the permission name checked (string) for traceability.

Chloe Martin: Current plan is to gate behind suggestions_beta feature flag + allowlist, and permission “optimize:suggestions:read” (new). PR-18695 adds the check.

Connor O'Brien: Release note: please keep event names stable if we expect enterprise audit exports. If we change them post-beta, that’s messy. Prefer final-ish naming now.

Logan Wright: Naming suggestion (no pun):
- audit.optimize_suggestions.list.view
- audit.optimize_suggestions.detail.view
- audit.optimize_suggestions.export
- audit.optimize_suggestions.access_denied

Logan Wright: And include schema_version of the suggestion payload in the audit event? Not sure that belongs in audit vs debug.

Naomi Feldman: I’d keep schema_version optional. It can help during incident investigations (“what did they see?”) but again: no numbers and no rationale bullets. Maybe a boolean “had_sensitive_fields=true/false” if we ever vary.

Marcus Lin: For “access_denied” audit: ensure we don’t log route/model from the attempted URL if it’s in query params. Safer to log just tenant + actor + action + reason=rbac.

Jada Williams: Implementation detail: in Console BFF, we can fire audit event after authz passes and after first successful fetch. For detail, we can use suggestion_id from the path (safe) and not log the full request.

Chloe Martin: Sounds like consensus:
1) Split audit logs into list view + detail view (+ export later)
2) Only log successful first fetch (dedupe) + also log access denied attempts
3) Payload: actor, tenant/workspace, suggestion_id for detail, action, permission checked. No numeric savings, no rationale, no basis-of-estimate window, no raw query strings.

Chloe Martin: I’ll update ENG-2408/PR-18695 follow-up with these specifics and ping @Kaitlyn @Naomi for quick review.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: :thumbsup: Please add a unit test that query params never flow into audit payload.

Naomi Feldman: :+1: And please confirm audit log retention matches our standard (90d default) and is scoped to the tenant admin audit log viewer role.

Allison Grant: Also add a metric for audit emit failures (drop on floor vs block request?). My vote: never block Suggestions UI due to audit pipeline; emit best-effort + alert.

Chloe Martin: Ack. Best-effort emit + warning log + counter. We won’t fail the user request.

Connor O'Brien: Great. Loop me in when ready for release train so we can update the rollout checklist.
